newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates steady, demand strong.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates steady, demand strong.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were staedy on Thursday despite a strong demand for kuna funds, dealers said.
"The banks' low liquidity was caused by their regular daily payments. Some banks have been asking borrowers to repay previous loans," dealer Jasenka Blagajic said.
Fresh borrowings totalled 45.7 million kuna with some five million kuna is still on offer and as much being sought.
So far, 38.7 million were placed in call money loans at an unchanged 10.5 percent.
Term deals were struck at 12 percent for one-week funds and 13 percent for two-weeks. One foreign bank granted a single five-day loan at 9.5 percent.
Wednesday's overnight trade totalled 11 million kuna that one bank sought to cover its shortfall. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
